key_idea: Visit columns in random order and only ask whether a column exceeds the current best height; binary search the exact height only when it does, which happens an expected H_w ~ 10 times.
sketch: Shuffle the columns. Keep best height B; for each column ask (x, B+1): one query that usually says sky. On 'building', binary search its height in [B+1, h] (60 queries for h = 1e18) and update B. The number of prefix-maximum records in a random permutation is ~ln(10000) ~ 9.8 with std ~3, so the total is about 10000 + 600 queries and 12000 leaves room for 33 records. Stop early if B = h (cannot query y = h+1); answer height 0 with any column if everything is sky. The interactor is non-adaptive so a time-seeded shuffle is safe. Samples cannot be checked by the token checker; validated with my own local interactor on random, all-zero, all-h and sorted (worst-case) skylines, max 10752 queries observed.
